an4.16:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of exquisiteness.
an4.16:1.3: (1) Here, a bhikkhu possesses supreme exquisiteness of form.
an4.16:1.4: He does not perceive any other exquisiteness of form more excellent or sublime than that one; he does not yearn for any other exquisiteness of form more excellent or sublime than that one.
an4.16:1.6: (2) He possesses supreme exquisiteness of feeling …
an4.16:1.13: He does not perceive any other exquisiteness of volitional activities more excellent or sublime than that one; he does not yearn for any other exquisiteness of volitional activities more excellent or sublime than that one.
an4.16:1.15: “These are the four kinds of exquisiteness.”
an4.16:2.1: Having known the exquisiteness of form,
an4.16:2.5: having known volitional activities as alien,
an4.16:2.6: as suffering, and not as self,
an4.16:3.1: truly that bhikkhu who sees rightly,
an4.16:3.2: peaceful, delights in the peaceful state.
an4.16:3.4: having conquered Māra and his mount.
